fault: The E key registers two keypresses every time it is pressed, which is a double-typing chattering switch.
safety_notes: Unplug the USB-C cable before pulling or inserting any switch.
Touch grounded metal or wear an anti-static strap before touching the PCB.
Pull and press the switch straight to avoid bending pins or damaging the socket.

steps.instruction: Unplug the USB-C cable from the back of the keyboard. Touch grounded metal before you reach in.
steps.expected_visual_state: No cable is in the USB-C port and the backlight is off.
common_mistakes: Leaving the cable plugged in while pulling switches.
Reaching for the board without grounding yourself first.

sources.title: How to Install Switches on Hot-Swap Keyboards – KeebsForAll

steps.title: Unplug the keyboard

steps.instruction: Hook the keycap puller under opposite edges of the E keycap and pull straight up. Set the keycap aside.
steps.expected_visual_state: The E keycap is off and the bare switch with its cross-shaped stem is visible.
common_mistakes: Pulling at an angle, which scratches the keycap or stresses the stem.

sources.title: How to Install Switches on Hot-Swap Keyboards – KeebsForAll

steps.title: Remove the E keycap

steps.instruction: Place the switch puller prongs on the top and bottom clips of the E switch, at plate level.
steps.expected_visual_state: The switch puller prongs rest on the top and bottom edges of the E switch, not the sides.
common_mistakes: Gripping the left and right sides so the switch will not release.
Placing the prongs high on the housing instead of at plate level.
steps.title: Grip the E switch

steps.instruction: Squeeze gently and pull the switch straight up in one steady motion.
steps.expected_visual_state: The old switch is in the puller and an empty square hole shows the socket underneath.
common_mistakes: Rocking the switch sideways, which damages the socket.
Pulling at an angle instead of straight up.
steps.title: Pull out the E switch

steps.instruction: Look into the empty E socket and blow out any dust with compressed air.
steps.expected_visual_state: The empty socket is clean with both pin holes clear and undamaged.
common_mistakes: Tilting the compressed air can upside down.
Poking the socket with metal tools.
steps.title: Clean the socket

steps.instruction: Hold up the spare switch and check both metal pins are straight.
steps.expected_visual_state: The spare switch is shown with two straight, undamaged pins.
common_mistakes: Using a switch with a bent pin without straightening it first.
steps.title: Check the spare switch

steps.instruction: Hold the spare switch over the E hole, facing the same way as its neighbours. Line its pins up with the socket holes.
steps.expected_visual_state: The new switch hovers level over the hole, oriented like its neighbours, with pins over the holes.
common_mistakes: Rotating the switch so the pins do not line up.
Holding the switch tilted so one pin enters first.
steps.title: Align the new switch

steps.instruction: Press the new switch straight down until it clicks into the plate.
steps.expected_visual_state: The new switch sits flush and level with the plate, matching its neighbours.
common_mistakes: Pressing at an angle and bending a pin.
Powering on with a tilted switch, which signals a misseated pin.

sources.title: How to Safely Replace RK61 Switches

steps.title: Press the switch in

steps.instruction: Line up the E keycap with the stem and press straight down until it is fully seated.
steps.expected_visual_state: The E keycap is back at the same height and angle as the surrounding keycaps.
common_mistakes: Not seating the keycap fully so it sits higher than the others.
steps.title: Put the keycap back

steps.instruction: Plug the cable back in and press the E key several times in a text editor. Check it types once per press.
steps.expected_visual_state: The cable is plugged in, the backlight is on, and one E appears per press on screen.
common_mistakes: Not testing the specific repaired key.
Not pressing repeatedly to check for double-typing.

title: E key switch replacement
diagnosis: A key that types twice is almost always a worn or dirty switch whose contacts bounce. I'll swap the E switch for a fresh one, since the keyboard is hot-swappable and needs no soldering.
